items.title: Byte models are becoming practical
items.oneliner: Byte-level language models are catching tokenized models at scale, which could finally kill tokenizer debt.

items.title: Google tested AMIE with real patients
items.oneliner: Google says AMIE matched doctors' final diagnosis lists 90% of the time in 98 urgent-care chats.

items.title: Small models can make calibrated decisions
items.oneliner: Constraining Qwen3-1.7B to fixed options turns generation into decisioning, which is far more useful for product workflows.

items.title: Researchers broke into Eufy doorbells
items.oneliner: Researchers extracted encrypted credentials from Eufy hardware and jammed connectivity, exposing how brittle consumer AI security remains.

items.title: Halifax leaked customer data again
items.oneliner: Halifax reportedly exposed card details to the wrong household again, a reminder that privacy failures are usually boring and repeatable.

items.title: Europe is moving on AI glasses
items.oneliner: Norway proposed banning AI glasses in some public spaces as schools and regulators start treating ambient recording seriously.

items.title: NumPy sped up searchsorted dramatically
items.oneliner: NumPy 2.5 makes searchsorted up to 25 times faster, which quietly accelerates histograms, interval lookups, and downstream ML stacks.

items.title: Logfire cut JSON query times hard
items.oneliner: Pydantic says dynamic shredding turned 30-second JSON queries into sub-second ones, a real win for observability at scale.

items.title: Rust got a span-aware heap profiler
items.oneliner: Culpert brings low-overhead heap profiling with tracing spans and CI regression checks, which is exactly how memory bugs get caught early.

items.title: The RAM shortage revived DDR4
items.oneliner: DDR5 prices got bad enough that Intel and AMD are reviving DDR4 paths, and infrastructure cost is steering architecture again.
